# DeckArt

Purpose: reusable assets for manufacturers' business presentations. Transparent PNG illustrations, opaque PNG backgrounds, and SVG icons, diagrams, charts and explanation parts. Japanese usage descriptions and Japanese/English search terms; stable English IDs. Assets and metadata: CC0-1.0. Code: MIT.

Entry to share: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sakurai-yoshi/deckart/main/llms.txt
Repository: https://github.com/sakurai-yoshi/deckart
Pinned raw base for this edition: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sakurai-yoshi/deckart/v2.1.1/

## Select, retrieve and compose

1. Identify what the slide needs to communicate. categories.json is a small overview of 14 business purposes, with index_path for each purpose. Each purpose index mixes relevant asset kinds. General charts and explanatory relationships are in catalogs/communication.json; abstract backgrounds are in catalogs/backgrounds.json and can accompany any business purpose. Browse one or more indexes, or use catalog.txt to scan every ID and title across the whole library. Consider illustrations, backgrounds, icons, diagrams, charts and explanation parts as appropriate to that purpose. Kind, format and recolor filters are optional choices, not defaults.
2. Compare candidates by use_case, message and keywords in the purpose indexes. catalog.json contains the complete index for local processing; catalog.ndjson has complete metadata for RAG. The category is the primary browsing purpose, not an automatic search filter. If another purpose may fit, include that index too. These describe examples and pictured meaning, not an allowed-use list. An asset can support other contexts that fit its appearance. Select assets for their contribution to the slide; there is no required quantity or category mix.
3. Open preview_path for candidates. If preview_has_example_labels=true, the preview includes example text to show how the diagram, chart or part communicates; those words can also be used directly when they fit the slide. Read metadata_path for the depicted relationships and available editing features. Choose from the image and the slide's content together. Illustrations' composition describes framing, facing and people count; it does not specify position or size.
4. Retrieve from the SAME pinned raw base and save response bytes with the declared format extension. For PNG and icons, download path and verify sha256. For a diagram or part, download preview_path and verify preview_sha256 when its example text fits the slide; this is a usable SVG with embedded text. Download path (verify sha256) for geometry to pair with your own text. For charts, render the actual data using the export tool below. PNG files live under media/; SVG geometry under assets/ and labeled SVGs under previews/. RAG bulk metadata is catalog.ndjson, one asset per line. Generation definitions under sources/ are historical production records; their prompts do not set conditions on using the artwork.
5. Compose around the actual text, data and visual hierarchy. Keep the image's proportions when scaling. Backgrounds can fill the slide, occupy part of it, or be cropped; a white panel or other overlay can improve text contrast. Position and size are decided in the presentation. View the rendered slide and adjust text fit, contrast, unintended overlaps, clipping and the meaning conveyed by the combination.

width/height describe pixels for PNG and viewBox units for SVG; canvas describes the asset's own coordinate system. These fields do not prescribe slide layout. transparent=true indicates PNG alpha; false indicates opaque PNG; null means SVG transparency is not classified. preview_path is a lightweight PNG preview, an SVG with example labels, or the original SVG where labels are unnecessary. preview_has_example_labels identifies labeled examples. SVG preview_sha256 verifies the labeled file. For SVG, path contains the geometry-only version, allowing freely placed text. PNG previews are reduced-size selection images; use the original path for final output.

CC0 permits editing, cropping and recoloring in your own software. The export tool's supported operations below describe its capabilities, not restrictions on using the artwork.

## Local search and export

Python 3.10+ and a repository checkout or unpacked release ZIP are sufficient. No package, account or API key is needed.

Search by purpose in Japanese or English. Related candidates are ranked; filters are optional. The default page has 20 results. Use next_offset for the next page, or --limit 0 for all matches. Review alternatives across kinds when the subject supports more than one visual treatment.

    python3 scripts/library.py search '品質改善の流れを説明する'
    python3 scripts/library.py search 'quality improvement' --offset 20
    python3 scripts/library.py search '' --limit 0
    python3 scripts/library.py show illustration/explaining
    python3 scripts/library.py export illustration/explaining --output ./exports/explaining.png
    python3 scripts/library.py export background/cover-prismatic-depth --output ./exports/cover.png
    python3 scripts/library.py export icon/person --accent '#005BAC' --output ./exports/person.svg
    python3 scripts/library.py export process/approval-return --example-labels --output ./exports/approval-preview.svg
    python3 scripts/library.py export --request examples/progress-data.json --output ./exports/progress.svg

Search returns UTF-8 JSON with total, returned, next_offset, filters and assets. Show returns detailed metadata. Export writes an image plus a JSON sidecar and returns file, format, mime_type, metadata, sha256 and render. The sidecar records the exported file and its hash. Its path and preview_path refer to the local exported file; source.path and source.preview_path resolve against source.raw_base and retain the original hashes. For PNG, generation.definition_path identifies its production record in that source edition. --stdout emits image bytes. Existing output files require --force. Errors return JSON on stderr and exit code 2.

The gallery’s individual card save follows the example-text visibility setting for SVGs with labels. Gallery ZIPs include both geometry-only SVGs and labeled SVG previews in the selected theme. Their catalog and metadata use path/sha256 for the geometry file and preview_path/preview_sha256 for the labeled file; source preserves references to the original edition. PNGs keep their original pixels.

## Export capabilities

request.schema.json defines id, optional format (matching the source), accent, monochrome, labels, include_example_labels and data. metadata.render describes each asset's supported operations.

- PNG: copies the original file and alpha. Recoloring, drawing text into the image, data rendering and format conversion are outside this tool. False monochrome/include_example_labels and empty labels leave the image unchanged. Add text separately in the presentation or edit the image with your own software.
- SVG theme: default blue, arbitrary #RRGGBB accent or monochrome. Semantic signal colors remain distinct. Pale brand colors are adjusted for contrast; resolved colors and adjustments are returned. See themes.json.
- SVG labels: an optional way to include text inside the exported SVG. metadata.labels lists label-N IDs, internal boxes, font sizes and text limits. Supply labels such as {"label-1":"申請","label-2":"確認"}. The tool reports text that exceeds those boxes. Write the slide's actual text freely in PowerPoint, or use labels when it fits the supplied geometry. With a data request, include_example_labels=true adds the labels computed from that data. SVG text uses the listed system-font fallbacks; geometry-only export has no font dependency.
- SVG charts: distributed values are sample data. Repeated-row/column charts accept variable category counts and expand their canvas to preserve label space. Read the exported width/height when placing them. metadata.data_input describes supported inputs. Export recalculates geometry and numeric labels together; supplied values are marked is_sample=false.

Use one tag or commit consistently for lookup, metadata and original image bytes. A modified export records both its output hash and its source so the final file remains traceable.
